column8: Tue 17 Nov: aha setting, claim 1; true for magic-trick solvers who found the answer themselves, so never read the 12 points as a judge's gain or the gap to the next team's report; rows 4-5 (shown answers) are the report's case.

Tue 17 Nov: register process guard: a felt aha is no truth check (75 of 329 wrong, Keel arithmetic on Danek's Table 1), so each spine row's truth check stays apart from its aha score; pairs with row 22.

Tue 17 Nov: aha setting; the certainty measured was the solver's own, not the text's tone, so the link to stating each fact flatly (Book 19) is Keel inference; say only that right answers held with certainty were remembered best and restructuring added nothing.

Tue 17 Nov: every spine row and Book 11: a shown answer after a brief attempt still gave an aha and better memory, so the report states each answer and asks nothing of the judge; never quote d = 0.96 as the aha's size (the controls were nonsense items).
Tue 17 Nov: sizes what Book 11's ban costs: a shown answer keeps a smaller aha benefit, a self-found one more; supports row 4, with the aha's own link to memory weak.
Tue 17 Nov: same lesson as row 4 (a watched reveal still sticks) on camouflaged pictures, with no told-cold baseline; row 4 carries it.
Tue 17 Nov: context only: the generation effect is the ceiling the report gives up under Book 11; word-level tasks, so no aha row changes.

Tue 17 Nov: UNVERIFIED (the 1983 paper read only as cited); a judge's unstated expectation is not an attempt to generate, so never call the judge fail-to-generate until the original or Brod et al. 2018 is read.
Tue 17 Nov: the original of row 10's delayed-key effect, its results read only as summarised; row 10 carries the verified table.

Tue 17 Nov: the sentence-scale recipe for all ten spine rows (puzzle sentence, key in the next, recall about doubled for lab sentences); drop the cold-test clause: Zaromb's readers were people, and simulated readers' ratings are no evidence of the same blindness.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.0 and CONCEIT V2.1: the frame before the rows (8.00 against 3.60 of 14 ideas) and a key held to a whole passage's end did nothing, so the definition stays before Table 1 and each aha's key sits in the next sentence.
Tue 17 Nov: conceit guard (V2.4): an irrelevant cue lowered recall below no cue, so a turn that fits a different mapping is worse than none, and a turn is never an aha's key sentence.

Tue 17 Nov: conceit (Book 19's startling new perspective): grasping a metaphor counts as insight and needs no impasse, so a defined turn can be a small aha; drop the leap from unconscious processing to where evidence sits on the page.
Tue 17 Nov: aha setting: the ease of the last step is the felt aha, so each key sentence is short and plain; distinct from Q14b-009 (fluency of a whole text).

Tue 17 Nov: aha targets and the conceit: curiosity rises with knowledge, so each aha opens a gap in finance (confidence, diversification, funding at market) and each cross-field turn serves that gap, as CONCEIT V2.4 guard 2 already asks.

Tue 17 Nov: Book 11 answered: a stated fact that breaks an expectation (trigger 3) opens the gap with no question; drop the trigger-4 mapping, since the judge sees the construction lines co-sponsors never do, so it opens no gap for the judge.
Tue 17 Nov: aha targets: a judge sure of the answer feels no gap, so naming the belief's real holder lets the judge notice they share it, with the gap one sentence wide (pairs with row 39).
Tue 17 Nov: register row 3 (2.5): satisfied curiosity tends to disappoint, so a one-sentence setup closed at once by its figure; the evidence is anecdotal.
Tue 17 Nov: aha targets: curiosity peaks near 50% sure, so half-held beliefs (the usual reading of a confidence level, diversification) suit spine rows 1 and 2; 16 people, figures only in a chart.

Tue 17 Nov: aha targets: confident errors are corrected more once shown wrong, so a confidently held expert belief is the best target; drop the cold-test field, since a simulated reader's stated confidence is not a person's.
Tue 17 Nov: the register's told once: confident errors returned when the fact was forgotten, so each aha's figure may recur once plainly (a table cell, a later number), never as a second aha.

Tue 17 Nov: guard for every aha and the conceit: an induced aha raised the felt truth of false claims as much as true ones, so every aha stands on its own NUMBERS figure and a turn is never the evidence; drop row 5b's 2.3 (simulated readers, not judges) and never use it to bring back certainty guards (Book 19).
Tue 17 Nov: UNVERIFIED (title only); the same lesson as row 22, which was read.
Tue 17 Nov: context only: felt insight is usually right for solvers, which is why readers trust it; it licenses no unchecked aha.
Tue 17 Nov: claim 3: refutation (the belief, why it misleads, the fact) is the tested form for setting each spine row; row 26 gives the adult size.

Tue 17 Nov: every spine row: g = 0.33 for university readers, and it works only on a misconception really held, so each aha names a belief someone real holds (a rule, a court, an industry figure), never a straw one.
Tue 17 Nov: register setting: no widespread backfire across 76 studies, so each row may state the wrong belief once without planting it.

Tue 17 Nov: UNVERIFIED (Paynter et al. read only as reported); the nearest evidence to expert readers says a refutation can fade, which backs row 21's plain recurrence; read the paper before leaning on it.
Tue 17 Nov: store; older readers gain less (the grade-11 finding UNVERIFIED, second-hand); row 26's verified university figure does the job.
Tue 17 Nov: CONFLICTING (original not read, effect sizes cannot be assigned); its conflict lesson is carried by rows 25 and 16.

Tue 17 Nov: the order for each register row: a pithy fact leads (row 2), a subtle one starts from why the belief misleads (row 1), each ends on its fact; repeat the fact yields to told once through row 21.

Tue 17 Nov: the register's density rule: unusual items are remembered only beside plain ones, so about one aha a page with plain ground between, and the range paragraph between spine rows 1 and 7 in 3c.
Tue 17 Nov: the same mixed-list lesson as row 32, from humour; row 32 carries it.

Tue 17 Nov: Book 18 backed by research: an aha that does no part's job is a seductive detail; UNVERIFIED (press release only, read the paper for its size), and drop the cold test 3 failures as examples (simulated readers' scores, failed for repetition).

Tue 17 Nov: aha ethics from detective fiction: every figure the key needs is on the page before it, so never a puzzle the report cannot answer truthfully; disanalogy recorded (a report never withholds for chapters).
Tue 17 Nov: CONFLICTING (book not read; the page read says the question is written out); use SCQA only as complication then answer, never as Minto backing an unwritten question.
Tue 17 Nov: holder, fallacy, fact is a sound template for every spine row from rows 25-31; drop the claim that this is why row 5 scored 4.3 (three simulated readers' scores are not reader evidence).

Tue 17 Nov: 3f, register row 10: set the aha on a belief a judge holds (a crash is the danger) so the judge's correction and the team's 27 Sep change land together; untested, so drop the causal claim from simulated scores, and keep the team's own reason from its record (standing order 21).
Tue 17 Nov: every spine row: name the belief's real holder, never you or many think; fix its own row 3 example (the reader's own sense is a you holder): give row 3 a real holder or set it plainly.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse: it treats simulated readers as people (filler items as a week's delay, a model's stated confidence as hypercorrection, its recall as memory); the human findings in rows 10, 20 and 21 cannot be measured on simulated readers.
